why: One $16k grant to TheatreWorks USA for theater for young people and families, but its other grants are mostly small general contributions (median $500).
Rochester youth arts and youth-services giving (Garth Fagan Dance2B program, Flower City Arts Center; arts is its top cause, FY2023), but no theater grants appear.
All 7 grants are on topic (children's theater, teen and youth programs, a theater facility) in PA, latest FY2023, though they are small (median $750).
Only 2 grants in five years, both to Broadway industry bodies (The Broadway League, Museum of Broadway), with no giving to community theater groups.
Six small recent grants (FY2025) pay licensing and production fees for junior and senior high school theater, mostly via the Education Theatre Foundation: school rather than community theater.
Only 4 grants (FY2024): Founders Fund grants to children's theaters (Free Play Society, Imagination Stage) and conference support for TYA/USA; on topic but thin.
Grants through FY2025 fund family-oriented productions and youth tickets at the Lewis Family Playhouse, local repertory theater productions and seed money for a new theatre company.
Only 3 grants (latest FY2023), all travel subsidies for community theaters attending its YouthFest; related but thin.
Recent youth arts giving (youth art initiatives, arts education) includes $30k to Young People's Theater and $25k to Adrian Center for the Arts, latest FY2024.
Very large general donor (1,320 grants, mostly 'general donation') whose visible arts giving is film preservation and major institutions; no youth or community theater evident.
